front.title: Scientific Constitutional Law for Evidence-Bound AI Systems: A Fail-Closed Claims and Authority Profile

abstract.t:
This document describes an experimental evidence-governance profile for scientific claims consumed by automated and AI-assisted systems. It separates claim content, evidentiary evaluation, provenance, integrity, and operational authority. Its three-valued evaluation state (PASS, FAIL, INDETERMINATE) and separate authorization decision prevent signed records, citations, or computational checks from being automatically promoted into scientific truth or legal authority. It proposes immutable versions, scope-bound receipts, monotonic source generations, transitive revocation, authenticated freshness, and adversarial conformance cases.
"Scientific Constitutional Law" is the name of the proposed procedural rule set; it is not a statement of enacted constitutional law, legal enforceability, scientific discovery, or IETF consensus. This document does not define a general truth engine or request IANA allocations.
